review_stale.does: Lets your AI assistant manage your Obsidian notes for you: it can read and search your notes, check them for broken links and missing info, suggest where new notes belong, pull readable text from web pages you give it, and make edits to your notes through a preview-then-approve step instead of changing files directly.
review_stale.scope: 10 file(s), 40.0KB read: skills/wiki-cli/SKILL.md, skills/wiki-lint/SKILL.md, skills/wiki-mode/SKILL.md, skills/obsidian-markdown/SKILL.md, +6 more. AGENTS.md truncated at 4KB of 5KB. 41 further file(s) NOT read — repo exceeds the 40KB review cap
review_stale.limits: This review is based on reading the source, not running it — nothing was executed, installed, or observed working. It covers only part of the repo: 41 files were withheld because the repo exceeds the review size cap, and one instruction file (AGENTS.md) was cut off partway through. Critically, the withheld files include all of the actual programs these instructions run — the Python and shell scripts (claude-obsidian.py, detect-transport.sh, retrieve.py, wiki-mode.py, and others) that do the real reading, writing, and web fetching. The instruction files reviewed describe a careful, safety-conscious design: edits are confined to your selected notes vault and go through a preview-and-approve step, web access is limited to one optional page-cleaning skill and requires your explicit consent each time, and the assistant is told to treat note contents as data rather than commands. But whether the unseen scripts actually behave that way could not be verified from what was provided. The web-fetch feature also relies on a separate 'defuddle' program the author does not ship; what that program does when installed is outside this review. No uninstall or removal instructions appear anywhere in the files reviewed.
review_stale.stale_reason: upstream HEAD moved from a3b3df45 to 1c1bc49c; the review described code that is no longer what a visitor would install
